title: Master Performer Protocol
opening: Use MPP when the work is to perform or apply an ability. Prepare for the task, do the whole performance, then review what it showed. Save component practice for a specific gap the performance exposed.

labels.taskHelp: Choose an actual competition, presentation, demonstration or other occasion where you will apply an ability. The lesson records your plan and review; it does not perform the task for you.
labels.noTask: Name the performance and its purpose before you begin.
labels.safety: If the conditions change in a way that affects safety or makes the task unsuitable, respond to that change. Preserving the whole task does not mean ignoring necessary adaptation.

prepare.label: Prepare for the actual task
prepare.description: State what the performance is for and what relevant conditions, equipment and readiness you need. Choose what real result or feedback you will inspect afterward. Preparation supports the performance; it does not prove its result.

perform.label: Keep the performance whole
perform.description: Set this lesson aside and complete the task as a whole. Respond to material conditions when needed. Do not stop after each moment to turn the task into an automatic series of isolated drills. Return here when the performance ends.

review.label: Review what happened
review.description: Compare the actual performance with its purpose and the evidence you chose. Record what it did and did not test. Keep a felt impression separate from observable task results; one performance does not prove every component is mastered.

practice.prediction: What is the performance, what is it for, and what ability will you apply?
practice.observation: What preparation, conditions, equipment or readiness matter for this occasion? Include a relevant earlier observation if you have one; otherwise say what you will observe.
practice.comparison: What real result, feedback or task evidence will help you judge whether the performance met its purpose?
practice.result: What happened in the whole performance? Record the task result and any felt impression separately. Say what remains unknown.
practice.revision: What specific gap, if any, did the whole performance expose? Describe the evidence. If none is clear, leave component practice unassigned.
practice.step: If a specific gap warrants it, what later component practice would address it? When will you return to the whole task to see whether that gap remains?

branches.whole: Optimal Performance Protocol (OPP) is the whole preparation, session and post-session arrangement. Master Learner Protocol (MLP) is OPP's learning version.
branches.performance: Master Performer Protocol (MPP) carries relevant preparation and post-session work into a performing or applying session. Its middle remains the whole performance.
branches.creation: Master Creator Protocol (MCP) is a distinct creating use/branch. It is not another name for MPP. A component practice can follow review when the performance exposed a specific gap.

feedback.unavailable: Private practice saving is unavailable. Your record remains on screen.
feedback.missing: Complete all six record fields before saving, or keep your notes on screen.
feedback.readFailure: The saved record could not be loaded. Your current work remains on screen.
feedback.conflict: This record changed elsewhere. Your answers remain here; compare the saved record before saving again.
feedback.readbackFailure: The save could not be confirmed. Retry to check the same save.
feedback.saveFailure: The save is uncertain. Retry to check the same save.
feedback.retryPending: The earlier save is unresolved. Retry the same answers before changing them.

source.distinctions: OPP is the whole protocol; MLP is OPP's learning version; MPP carries relevant preparation and review around whole performance; MCP is the distinct creating use/branch.
source.limits: The presenter example is source illustration, not an observed learner result. A self-report does not establish task performance. A recorded result under one set of conditions does not prove every component or establish a cause. Specific preparation settings and physiological claims are not universal doses or established performance multipliers.
